newsitem.title: FRANCE: French audit says 97 deficit in 3.5-3.7 pct range.
newsitem.headline: French audit says 97 deficit in 3.5-3.7 pct range.

text.p: An audit of French public finances found that the 1997 public deficit is running at between 3.5 and 3.7 percent of gross domestic product, auditor Jacques Bonnet said on Monday.
Bonnet was speaking to reporters after presenting a report by two experts from the state Court of Auditors to Prime Minister Lionel Jospin.

Asked what figure they had given for the public deficit in 1997, the reference year for meeting the Maastricht treaty goal of three percent to qualify for a single European currency, he said: "3.5-3.7, we give a range."
Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn was due to announce the full findings of the audit and a package of tax and savings measures at a news conference at 10.30 a.m. (0830 GMT).
Government sources said the main measure would be an increase in corporate tax on big business aimed at bringing this year's deficit down to within reach of the three percent target.
